newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada slips on higher Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada slips on higher Q4 loss.

text.p: Shares of Air Canada slipped 0.10 to 7.80 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday morning, after the airline reported that its fourth-quarter loss widened from the year earlier period.

Air Canada reported a fourth-quarter loss of C$18 million or C$0.14 a share, compared with a loss of C$12 million or C$0.10 a share in the year earlier quarter. Revenues were C$1.2 billion in the latest quarter, versus C$1.1 billion a year earlier.
Air Canada's year-end results were also significantly lower than forecast by the company a year ago.

In February 1996, former Air Canada chairman, president and chief executive Hollis Harris forecast a 1996 net profit above C$100 million, before any gains. Air Canada reported a 1996 net profit of C$149 million, or C$0.82 a share, compared with C$62 million or C$0.36 a share in 1995.
The 1996 profit included a C$129 million gain on the sale of part of Air Canada's investment in Continental Airlines Inc. The airline had a 1995 gain of C$57 million.
Last February, Harris forecast an operating profit for 1996 of more than C$300 million, after C$275 million in 1995. The airline had a 1996 operating profit of C$215 million.
Analysts said the wider net loss for the latest fourth quarter and lower-than-forecast net and operating profits were expected because of higher one-time costs associating with operating the airline.

In the latest quarter, for example, fuel costs were C$36 million or 27 percent higher, while maintenance expenses rose C$21 million. Air Canada also incurred additional workforce training costs of C$6 million as it prepared for a fourth-quarter sales agents strike that never happened.
"If you look behind the numbers, it was a good quarter," said Jacques Kavafian, of Research Capital Corp.

Kavafian said he had expected Air Canada to lose C$16 million in the latest fourth quarter, compared with the C$18 million loss actually reported. He expects Air Canada to report a 1997 net income of about C$125 or C$0.80 a share.
In recent weeks, Air Canada shares have slipped from a 52-week high of C$8.45, which was reached on market perceptions of financial troubles at domestic competitor Canadian Airlines Corp.
Kavafian said he has a 12-month price target of C$12 for Air Canada shares.
